England vs New Zealand: Maro Itoje says Lewis Moody gave team 'lift' as former captain joins side to face Haka
Lewis Moody was invited onto the field to join England to face the Haka during England's 37-12 victory against New Zealand on Saturday; Maro Itoje said Moody's presence 'lifted' his team; Moody was diagnosed with MND in 2025 and is campaigning to raise awareness of the illness
Saturday 21 November 2026 19:12, UK
Maro Itoje said Lewis Moody gave England the boost they needed to beat New Zealand 37-12 as the former captain joined the team to face the Haka at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.
As the All Blacks prepared to perform the Haka, Itoje wandered to the touchline and welcomed Moody, who was diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease (MND) in September 2025, onto the field.
The 48-year-old, who won 71 caps for England, took up position at the point of England's arrow formation to accept the challenge from the All Blacks during Saturday's match.

- Nations Championship: Schedule, results for rugby's inaugural tournament
After the Haka, the England team all embraced Moody.
It was an emotional start to the match but Itoje believed having the "inspirational" former flanker on the pitch gave England a "lift".
"I got into playing rugby relatively late in comparison to a lot of my colleagues and I remember watching England play, particularly around 2011," Itoje said during his press conference.
"Lewis is such an inspirational man, he was an inspirational player and given his diagnosis, the players jumped at the opportunity to support him.
"He and his family gave us that extra lift today."
England subsequently got off to a flying start, with Henry Slade collecting a grubber kick from Fin Smith inside four minutes of kick-off to give England an early lead.
Moody had presented the England side with matchday jerseys at their Pennyhill Park base on Friday night.
"He came to spend some time with us yesterday," Itoje said.
"He presented us our shirts for today's game, he spoke to us, addressed us, and there's no doubt that his presence, him joining us for the Haka, him spending time with us, gave us an extra lift."
All of England's players wore specially customised boots that had the logo of Moody's 'Front Up to MND' campaign printed on them.
England players also signed and donated their warm-up tops and match jerseys.
Itoje said Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney called him a few weeks ago to discuss the idea about having the former British and Irish Lion join England for the Haka. The team fully supported the idea.
"I just remember his heroic performances for England, throwing his body in and around the team, and the way he played was inspirational," Itoje said.
"He was one of the guys that I looked up to as a young boy playing rugby.
"I have the honour and privilege of captaining this great team, and to be able to welcome him, to be able to receive him onto the field is a memory that's going to live with me for the rest of my life.
"As the England group, there are many players who've been particularly pertinent in supporting him, but just as an England group, we're just so proud to be able to support him and help him, and going forward, whatever we can do to help him and his family, we would love to."

שחקן נבחרת אנגליה, מארו איטג'ה, ציין כי נוכחותו של קפטן העבר לואיס מודי על כר הדשא העניקה לנבחרת דחיפה משמעותית בדרך לניצחון 37-12 על ניו זילנד. מודי, שחולה בניוון שרירים, הוזמן להצטרף לשחקנים מול ריקוד ההאקה המסורתי באצטדיון אליאנץ.

השחקנים קיבלו את פניו בהתרגשות לאחר שחלקו לו כבוד גם בהענקת החולצות ערב קודם לכן ובנקיטת צעדים להעלאת המודעות למחלתו. איטג'ה הדגיש כי הרגע המיוחד יישאר זכור לכל חברי הנבחרת למשך שארית חייהם.
